Unused variable behaviour.

In general, unused variables in tests should be removed unless their instantiation side effects are required. If only the constructor side effect is needed, the variable name can be dropped and the constructor can be called without assignment; if even that is unnecessary, the entire line can be removed.
For this specific case in apps/web/test/viewmodels/structures/auto-collapse/behaviours/CollapseOnWindowResizeBehaviour-test.ts, the "should return correct shouldStartCollapsed" test only checks the static shouldStartCollapsed() method, which does not depend on any particular instance created in that test. Therefore, we should remove the behaviour declaration entirely. The simplest and safest fix is to delete line 55:
const behaviour = new CollapseOnWindowResizeBehaviour(collapseHandler as unknown as CollapseHandler);

No new imports or other definitions are needed. The rest of the test remains unchanged and continues to validate the intended behavior.

The best fix is to delete the unused behaviour variable declaration on line 57 and also remove the now-unneeded ESLint suppression comment on line 56. This keeps the test focused on what it is actually exercising and eliminates the unused-variable warning. No changes to imports, other tests, or functionality are needed, and no additional methods or definitions are required.
Concretely, in apps/web/test/viewmodels/structures/auto-collapse/behaviours/CollapseOnWindowResizeBehaviour-test.ts, inside the it("should return correct shouldStartCollapsed", ...) block, remove the two lines that create collapseHandler and behaviour, and leave the rest of the test intact.
